newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on speculative buying.

text.p: Thai stocks closed higher in moderate dealings on Wednesday on speculative buying, brokers said.

"Investors bought some bank and building materials issues for speculative reasons amid concerns that some banks and finance firms may have to set up reserves for possible loan loss provision this year," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The SET index ended 4.79 points higher at 858.97 on 6.5 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 0.33 point to 64.52.
Advancers led decliners 176 to 135, excluding foreign shares, while 99 issues were unchanged.
An analyst at a foreign brokerage house said some medium and small-sized banks and finance firms may be forced to provide higher loan loss provision in the first quarter of this year.
"These banks and finance companies didn't make sufficient provisions in 1996. The pressure on the setting up of the reserves for loan loss provision will rise gradually," the analyst said.

The banking sector gained most in terms of value today, rising 1.39 percent, followed by the finance sector, which slipped 1.62 percent. The building and furnishing materials sector rose 2.76 percent.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 54.50 baht. National Finance and Securities slipped 0.50 to 50 after announcing yesterday that its net profit for 1996 dropped to 1.21 billion baht versus 1.5 billion baht in 1995. Large capitalised Siam Cement surged 16 to 852.
Support is seen by some brokers at 850 and resistance at 890 on Thursday. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
